h: Rollercoasters, zoos and the Golden Mile
p: AirHop sits in the south of Blackpool, which puts it handily close to South Shore and the Pleasure Beach, the amusement park whose big rollercoasters dominate that end of the skyline. Next door, Sandcastle Waterpark is an indoor waterpark with slides and pools, another great option if the weather turns. So, if the family has the energy, it's quite possible to bounce in the morning and ride in the afternoon, though you may need an early night afterwards.

Head inland and Stanley Park has a boating lake, Italian Gardens and a cafe, with Blackpool Zoo on its edge, home to elephants, big cats and much more. It's a calmer contrast to the bustle of the front. If you're visiting in the autumn, the Blackpool Illuminations light up miles of the promenade, a spectacle families have loved for generations.

Of course, no trip to Blackpool is complete without the arcades along the Golden Mile. They're packed with coin pushers, grabbers and classic seaside games, and there's a good mix of family-friendly amusements. Some venues along the front are adult gaming centres, which are 18+ only, so keep that in mind if you have youngsters with you. For a quieter change of pace, Lytham St Annes is just down the coast with its windmill, green and sandy beach. Blackpool can get very busy in peak season, so booking your AirHop session ahead is a sensible move, and the trams along the prom are a handy way to hop between all the fun without moving the car.
